A quiet but live loop shown as a hint is accepted. The turn this plugin's checkpoint nudge closes is no stop only in the nudge's [continue] form as the hook adds it (its [halt] sentence wins), and only when that turn asks the user nothing (sessions 40-44, 63); an agent woken by SendMessage is not ended by its earlier run's crossed notification (session 46). A queued prompt ends the loop's live context at its enqueue, but not a prompt the session scheduled itself, and a pause asked still holds until the prompt is delivered (sessions 47, 48, 57, 59, 60, 62); Claude Code's notice that the person stopped background agents is a stop (sessions 58, 61). Arguments that cannot be shown and hold more than the parts a re-enter command keeps give the hint (sessions 66-69: the command would re-enter a wider run). A queued notification of the loop's own makes the next turn's opener the loop's only by its own sender (sessions 56, 73-75). Sessions 76-84 guard what planted bugs got past. A Bash command that names phase.complete in a form the gsd-tools parser does not read (through a variable, a flag before the verb, a quoted or variable phase) ends a single-phase loop, and a bounded run when it names its last phase or one that cannot be read (sessions 95-100, also after a gate); a row too long to read that may open a turn (a pasted prompt, typed or queued) is unclear, a long tool result or a long row of another type is not (sessions 101-104). A prompt with only an image or a document is a prompt, queued or not (sessions 105-108); a prompt queued mid-turn whose text starts with a tag that is no notification counts from its enqueue (sessions 109-111); the phase.complete forms of sessions 112-114; arguments hidden only by quotes keep a letter phase (session 115); a long enqueue in any key order, a long message of another session and a long notification of the loop's own work are unclear, the last also for the loop invoked again, while a long sidechain row or a long meta row of Claude Code's own is not (sessions 116-120).
